Title: SQL Injection via Unsanitized substring parameter in PostgreSQL locate function
Analysis:
Under PostgreSQL dialect, the `locate` function translates into the SQL `POSITION` function. However, instead of parameterizing or properly escaping the user-provided `substring` string, the library directly appends it to the constructed SQL string using raw string concatenation inside the `PostgreSQLFunctionProvider.locate` method. This allows an attacker who controls the `substring` parameter to inject arbitrary SQL statements.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
Suppose a developer executes the following query:
`Cities.selectAll().where { Cities.name.locate(userInput) eq 1 }`
With `userInput` set to:
`' IN name) > 0 OR 1=1; --`
The generated SQL query becomes:
`SELECT * FROM cities WHERE POSITION(\'' IN name) > 0 OR 1=1; --\' IN name) = 1`
This causes the SQL interpreter to parse `OR 1=1;` and ignore the rest of the statement, effectively returning all entries in the `cities` table regardless of the original filter condition.
